body.statement: Uniformly over the bounded radius regime \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\) and the fixed reservoir-rich shell constants, with every minimax infimum taken over \(T\in\mathcal T_n\) measurable in the observed sample and allowed to use \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), and the certified radii, \(\mathfrak R_n^{(1)}\asymp\rho_n\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\asymp\rho_n\), and \(\mathfrak R_{n,\delta}^{(\mathrm{prob})}\asymp\rho_n\) for every fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\). Thus the same \(\rho_n\) is the sharp frontier for absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, and fixed-probability error.
body.justification: It closes the exact global-prediction price of one-sided weak overlap across three operational loss criteria.
body.gap: The closest regular-overlap benchmarks are JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE; no located weak-overlap paper has this matched public-function frontier.
body.consumer: Method developers can use the theorem as the oracle benchmark for clipping, robustification, and any proposed higher-order correction.
